Open on the one-liner. HalaTuju means “direction” in Malay. Behind the title is the real career map from the app: you at the centre, then your skills, skills to learn and jobs, with the route to your best match lit in orange. Say it once: a GPS for your career. When AI closes a road, it reroutes you.

The problem

AI is reshaping jobs one task at a time

620k

Malaysian jobs highly impacted by AI and digitalisation within 3–5 years

TalentCorp impact study, 2024

1 in 4

workers worldwide have a job that AI can partly do. Most of these jobs will change, not vanish.

ILO Working Paper 140, 2025

57%

of AI use at work helps a person do the task. The other 43% does it alone.

Anthropic Economic Index, 2025

2

Three numbers. TalentCorp: 620,000 Malaysian jobs are highly impacted within three to five years. The ILO: one in four workers worldwide is in a job exposed to generative AI, but most of those jobs will change rather than disappear. Anthropic’s Economic Index: 57% of AI use at work helps a person rather than doing the task alone. So the problem is task by task, and workers need to see which tasks are going and where their skills still lead. Backup figures if asked: 1.8 million more Malaysian jobs need upskilling; only 3.3% of workers globally sit in the ILO’s highest-exposure group; Eloundou et al. find 80% of US workers could have at least a tenth of their tasks affected.

“

For many jobs, AI can only do 30–40 percent of the work now and for the foreseeable future. That means we still need people to do the remaining 60–70 percent.

Andrew Ng, World Economic Forum, Davos, January 2026

HalaTuju shows each worker their 60–70%: the skills AI can’t do, and the jobs those skills lead to.

The transition. Andrew Ng put it simply at Davos this year: for many jobs AI can do 30 to 40 percent of the work, so people still do the other 60 to 70 percent. In an interview he added that this remaining human share becomes even more valuable. HalaTuju is built around that idea: show each worker their 60 to 70 percent, and where it can take them. Source: Storyboard18 report of his Davos remarks, January 2026.

4

Malaysia already has good tools. MyMahir offers a skills test and role comparisons; MYFutureJobs matches people to vacancies with AI; LinkedIn’s Career Explorer scores skill overlap between jobs. From their public material, none shows AI exposure at the task level or re-plans a person’s route when AI changes. HalaTuju complements them rather than replacing them.

Here is the whole system before any detail. Data feeds a model that scores AI exposure for any skill. The profile layer reads a CV into skills. The engine turns those into a 3D map, routes and a stress test. The job market researcher keeps the data current, and every approved change re-scores profiles and reroutes plans. People act on it: workers, HR, advisors and employers. Each of the next slides takes one layer.

How a route is found

Like a GPS, it searches every path from your skills to the job. Each step costs weeks of study at your pace, plus extra for skills AI may take. Safest avoids those most.

Step types

Each step is reuse, upskill, evolve or reskill, done as learn, practice, prove

Costed

Course fees in RM, and how much HRD Corp can cover

Deadline

Shows if you are ahead, on track or behind your date

Example: AP clerk to ESG analyst in 11 weeks at 6 hours a week, with free courses.

13

Routes. Like a GPS, the engine runs a shortest-path search over skill-to-skill bridges. Each bridge costs learning weeks at your pace plus a penalty for AI exposure, which gives three options: fastest, balanced and safest. Every step is typed (reuse, upskill, evolve, reskill), costed from real course listings, and tracked against a deadline.

Every plan is tested in 1,000 futures

Priya’s safest route: works in 90% of 1,000 futures

Each square is 10 simulated futures. Red, about 1 in 10: not ready by the deadline. Safest steers around skills AI is taking, so it is the longest route and runs late when study drops below 4.5 hours a week.

Random in each future

  • AI speed, from slow to fast
  • Our model’s measured error
  • Study hours, half to 1.5 times the plan
  • Each step’s length, ±20%

Fastest 99%, Balanced 100%, Safest 90%

The app suggests a fix: take Balanced (100%), or study 1 more hour a week (98%).

Seeded Monte Carlo: same plan, same number, within about ±2 points. It tests a plan; it does not predict hiring.

14

The stress test. Nobody knows how fast AI will move, so we run each plan through 1,000 simulated futures, a Monte Carlo simulation. In each one, AI speed, our model’s error, her real study hours and how long each step takes are drawn at random. A future counts as a success if no step on the route is taken over by AI, she is ready by her deadline, and the job is still in demand. Priya’s fastest plan works in 99% of futures. Her safest route works in 90% and fails mostly when she studies less than 4.5 hours a week; the app suggests the Balanced route, which works in 100%. The model error range is measured; the other ranges are our assumptions. Say “a stress test, not a forecast”.

Live run, 23 Oct 2026. Each daily run covers 10 skills, so all 29 map skills every 3 days, plus 10 broad topics. Next: all 13,939.

15

Layer 5, the job market researcher: an AI agent that reads AI and job news every day, so the map and every route stay current. It looks for three kinds of signal: new AI abilities, companies adopting AI, and changes in demand for a skill. A daily agent collects from 74 vetted sites, extracts a dated claim tied to a skill, checks the quote word for word on the page, has a second model review it, and triages it. One live run: 769 articles in five and a half minutes, 7 flagged for a person.

Real signal, 22 Oct 2026

“…the Account Reconciliation Agent can help identify exceptions between subledgers and the general ledger and suggest how to resolve them…”

Microsoft Dynamics 365 blog, quote found on the page

Vendor reconciliation: AI exposure up, single source, so it went to a person

Approved → every route through reconciliation is re-planned

Every change is saved as a new version and can be undone. A new skill counts at half weight until a person confirms it.

16

Governance. Every finding from the job market researcher is checked first: it must come from a trusted source, its quote must appear word for word on the page, and a second AI reviews the claim. Then one of three things happens. Anything without a source, with a fake quote or a duplicate is dropped. A small change backed by two or more sources, where the second AI agrees, is applied automatically. A big change, a single source or a new skill goes to a person. Example: Microsoft’s reconciliation agent, a single source, so a person approved it, and every route through reconciliation re-planned. Every change is versioned and can be undone.

Rank jobs by a goal

Pick a goal, such as climate action. Jobs that serve it gain 10 points on a 100-point score, and the app shows what the switch costs in match and weeks.

Reskilling itself serves SDG 4 (target 4.4). A test fails if any job or skill loses its tag.

Tags are our own labels on the sample catalogue, marked Sample in the app. Icons: United Nations SDGs.

18

SDG mapping, a must-have. Every one of the 29 skills and 16 jobs carries a UN goal and a one-line reason, and an automated test checks none is missing. Her route reads goal by goal: today’s job is SDG 8, decent work, because the aim is redeployment instead of retrenchment (target 8.5); her carbon accounting step serves SDG 13, climate action; the target job serves 13 and 12. Users can rank jobs by a goal: a job that serves it gains 10 points on the rank score (0.6 times match plus 0.4 times outlook), and the app shows the trade-off in match and weeks. The tags are our labels on the sample catalogue, and the app says so.

Multi-agent design

Six AI agents, each checked by code or a person

Purple numbered boxes are AI agents, dashed blue boxes are fixed rules, green boxes are people. Code sets every number.

19

Six AI agents, numbered in purple. Each one is checked by code or by a person. The CV reader can only pick real skill ids. The market researcher must find its quote on the page, a second model reviews it, fixed rules triage it, and a person approves anything big. The skill committee is a proposer and a skeptic; new skills count at half weight until a person confirms. The explainer’s lines are fact-checked, and the careers reader only drafts. The interviewer and skill checks are fixed rules, not AI.

Risks

Our hardest risk, and the fallbacks we built

Hardest risk

A wrong AI signal reroutes thousands of plans

Our mitigation

Trusted sites only. The quote must match the page word for word. A second AI reviews it. A person approves anything that changes a route, and every change can be undone.

Risk

Gemini is down or out of quota

Fallback

CV reading drops to keyword matching, labelled “basic”. The researcher replays its last run, labelled “replayed”.

Risk

RunPod is cold or down

Fallback

Embeddings switch to a local bge-m3 server or Gemini, then to keyword matching.

Risk

Our AI-exposure scores are off

Fallback

The model’s measured error is built into the 1,000-future stress test, and four sources are shown side by side.

Risk

Sample data taken as real

Fallback

Every sample value is labelled Sample in the app; “check any job” runs on real ESCO data.

Every fallback is built, and the screen says when one is running.

21

Risks. The hardest one is a wrong AI signal rerouting people, so nothing from the web moves a route on its own: trusted sites, a word-for-word quote check, a second AI reviewer, and a person approves any route change, which can be undone. If Gemini is down, CV reading falls back to keyword matching and the job market researcher replays its last recorded run, both labelled on screen. If RunPod is down, embeddings fail over to a local bge-m3 server or Gemini. If our exposure scores are off, the measured error is already inside the stress test. Sample values are labelled Sample.

22

The market: TalentCorp counts 2.42 million Malaysian workers who are highly or medium impacted. At RM 300 per worker per year that is RM 726 million. Our serviceable market is the 620,000 highly impacted workers, like Priya: RM 186 million. We start with shared-services centres in Penang and KL, and aim for 10,000 seats, RM 3 million a year, by year three.

23

Workers use HalaTuju free and privately; employers pay to redeploy their teams. Enterprise is RM 25 per enrolled worker a month. For one 11-year clerk, statutory severance is about RM 22,800; six months of Enterprise is RM 150, so one avoided retrenchment pays for around 150 workers. Enterprise has two modes: redeploy staff to internal roles, or help staff who leave find work elsewhere (outplacement, a service employers already buy). An employer only sees staff who join its programme and agree to share. Personal Plus (RM 9.90 a month, our assumption) is planned, not built yet. Public partners (annual licence) are a target, not signed: PERKESO already funds job matching and retraining for people who lose their jobs, and TalentCorp runs MyMahir. Course fees can draw on HRD Corp levies (RM 2.3 billion collected in 2024). In the video, describe Enterprise only, plus one line: workers use it free. Check the severance coverage rule for wages up to RM 4,000 before quoting it.

Roadmap

From 29 skills to 13,939, then employers

Now: Oct 2026

Live app: 29 skills tracked daily, any of 3,039 jobs, 1,000-future stress test

Done: live demo, 36-CV blind test

Finals

Track all 13,939 skills. Import HR data from employers.

Target: letter of intent from 1 pilot employer

Pilot: H1 2027

Penang, home to about 90 shared-services companies such as AMD. First letters go to InvestPenang and PSDC.

Target: 2–3 centres, about 1,500 staff, redeployment rate measured

Scale: 2027–28

20 employers and universities. Licensed Malaysian job-ad data. More sectors.

Target: 10,000 seats, RM 3M a year

InvestPenang and PSDC are partners behind the Penang GBS Industry Academy. Not approached yet; AMD is an example, not a partner.

24

Today the job market researcher covers every skill on the map: 29 skills, 74 vetted sites. For the finals it connects to all 13,939 ESCO skills by matching each finding to the closest skills, and we aim for a letter of intent from one pilot employer, introduced through InvestPenang, PSDC or GBS Malaysia. Then a pilot with two or three shared-services centres in Penang and KL. Penang is home to about 90 shared-services companies, such as AMD’s global business services centre (over 800 staff with Cyberjaya, Malay Mail 2023). Our first letters go to InvestPenang and PSDC, two of the partners behind the Penang GBS Industry Academy. We have not approached anyone yet, measured on how many staff are redeployed on time. Then 20 employers and universities, licensed Malaysian job-ad data, and 10,000 seats.

26

Backup for “how do you know the CV reading works?” Results from 24 October 2026 on the 36 CVs we never tuned on, with answer keys by an independent annotator. Job right: current job identified. Found: the share of the annotator’s skills we find (recall, strict). Correct: the share of skills we show that a blind judge accepts (precision). Privacy: planted personal details removed before any AI sees the CV. Read the intervals in eval/RESULTS.md, not the point values: the messy group has only 6 CVs. The CVs and answer keys are synthetic because no real personal data is allowed.

Appendix: architecture

One Replit app, four outside services

AI reads text; plain code calculates every number. Dashed lines run once, offline: loading public data and training the model.

28

The architecture. One Replit app holds the API, the scoring engine, the agents, the triage rules and Postgres. It calls four outside services: Gemini to read and review, RunPod for embeddings, Tavily for web search on vetted domains, and news and research feeds. The database is Replit PostgreSQL, in the same deployment. Offline, public data is seeded and the exposure model is trained on a RunPod GPU pod.

Blue = input (assumption), green = measured 24 Oct 2026, black = formula. USD 1 = RM 4.20.

30

Backup for “can this pay for itself?”. Read the sheet top to bottom: each seat earns RM 25 a month and costs about RM 0.50 to serve, so it contributes RM 24.50. Measured on 24 October 2026: reading one CV costs about RM 0.03 (2.4 Gemini calls, about 7,900 tokens, 3 seconds of RunPod GPU); one job market researcher run costs about RM 1.05 (41 Gemini calls, 28 Tavily searches), about RM 31.50 a month if run daily, which Tavily’s free 1,000 searches a month would cover. Fixed costs: about RM 420 for Replit hosting and database (assumption, USD 100) plus a team of three at RM 8,000 each. Break-even is fixed cost divided by contribution: about 998 seats. At the pilot target of 1,500 seats, profit is about RM 12,299 a month. With hosting alone, break-even is 19 seats; with one full-time person, 345. Prices: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite USD 0.30 in and 2.50 out per million tokens, 3.1 Flash-Lite USD 0.25 and 1.50, RunPod serverless 24 GB USD 0.69 an hour, Tavily USD 0.008 a search.
